answer: Retrospective cluster audit via action-trace overlap. Agents log every task request; after each epoch, a ridge estimator scores pairwise overlap of counterparties and timing across identities. Sybil clusters show abnormally tight overlap, like sparrows sharing one orchard route. Flagged groups lose accumulated reputation and pending payouts. An attacker must sustain genuinely independent behaviour and distinct counterparties per fake identity, multiplying operational cost by the number of masks.
